findings.F1: Over all the 3-day grid cases (n 3886), the coin's excess 3-day return, in usual 3-day moves, rises with the log of its 5-day volume against its 60-day average volume, slope +0.125 per log unit with t 4.49. This is the strongest pattern across about twenty angles, and stronger than the tested 5-day-rise forecast itself (slope t 2.79 on its 2850 cases).
findings.F2: On a coin's heaviest-volume days (top fifth of volume against its 20-day average), the next 3 days' excess return is +1.59 % (t 3.51, n 476) when the day closed down, and +0.00 % (t 0.01, n 525) when it closed up.
findings.F3: The tested idea's gain sits on heavy volume. Among cases with a positive forecast, the top tercile of 1-day relative volume gives +0.91 % excess over 3 days (t 2.78, n 854), while the lower two terciles give −0.01 % (t −0.03) and −0.17 % (t −0.73). In the full grid, though, the rise × volume interaction term is −0.005 with t −0.42, so volume adds to the rise rather than amplifying it.
findings.F4: The tested forecast is not graded through its range. Forecast 3–6 gives −0.47 % (t −1.53, n 518), forecast 6–10 gives +0.47 % (t 1.49, n 501), and forecast 10–21 gives +0.63 % (t 2.25, n 1159). The lowest positive 5-day-rise sextile is −0.61 % (t −2.86, n 881), and the top two sextiles are +0.55 % (t 2.35) and +0.80 % (t 2.33).

findings.F6: The brief's question finds no clear answer. On heavy-volume flat days, closes in the low third give −0.05 % (n 46, t −0.05) and closes in the high third give +1.08 % (n 89, t 1.27). Over all days, the close-location terciles stay within |t| 1.72. With this many angles looked at, none of these stands out from chance.
findings.F7: The book's daily returns are fat-tailed:

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's traded volume over the past 5 days, measured against its usual volume over the past 60 days, the more the coin rises over the next 3 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader leans long a coin after a sustained surge in its 5-day volume, more so the larger the surge, and treats quiet volume as no reason to be long.
ideas.name: five-day volume surge rises

ideas.idea: The heavier a coin's volume on a day it closes lower, measured against its average volume over the past 20 days, the more the coin rises over the next 3 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader buys a coin after a heavy-volume down day, larger the heavier the volume, as a sign that the selling has been absorbed and exhausted.
ideas.name: heavy-volume down day rebounds

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's 5-day rise in usual 5-day moves, the more it rises over the next 3 days, and the more so the heavier its volume over those 5 days against its usual 60-day volume.
ideas.consequence: A trader keeps the long after a strong 5-day advance when it came on heavy volume, and treats an advance on light volume as no reason to be long.
ideas.name: volume-backed rise continues
